implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py defines DIFFICULTIES = {"Beginner": (9,9,10), "Intermediate": (16,16,40), "Expert": (16,30,99)} and gui.py creates an OptionMenu populated with these keys.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player uncovers cells by clicking on them
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py creates a Button for each cell with command=lambda r=r, c=c: self.on_reveal(r, c) which calls Minesweeper.reveal(r,c).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate how many mines are adjacent
implemented_requirements.evidence: Minesweeper._flood sets cell.revealed and cell.adjacent is computed in place_mines; gui.refresh displays str(cell.adjacent) when cell.revealed.

implemented_requirements.requirement: If a mine is uncovered, the player loses
implemented_requirements.evidence: Minesweeper.reveal checks if cell.mine, sets self.state = "lost" and reveals all mines; gui.refresh shows a mine symbol and status_label "Boom! You uncovered a mine...".
After every reveal or flag action, gui.refresh iterates over all cells and updates button text, background, and relief.
gui.refresh binds right‑click (Button-3) and middle‑click (Button-2) to on_flag which calls Minesweeper.toggle_flag; toggle_flag flips cell.flagged.
When cell.flagged, gui.refresh configures the button with text=FLAG_SYMBOL, bg=FLAG_BG ("#FFD54F"), and raised relief.

critical_issues: None observed that prevent core functionality. Minor: flags_used is incremented/decremented correctly, but the remaining_mines display may become negative if the player flags more cells than mines (not a fatal functional issue).
judge.summary: The provided code implements a fully functional classic Minesweeper game with three difficulty levels, click‑to‑reveal, adjacent mine counts, loss on mine, automatic board refresh, a flagging system, and a distinct visual for flagged cells. The logic and GUI are complete and appear ready to run, meeting all core benchmark requirements.
